items.reviewed_target: what is the relationship between premise:The tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL) pathway has emerged as a cancer therapeutic target. However, clinical trials have proven that most human cancers are resistant to TRAIL. We show that exposure to recombinant TRAIL resulted in the accumulation of ubiquitinated proteins and free ubiquitin polymers, suggesting a link between TRAIL and the ubiquitin (Ub)-proteasome pathway. TRAIL treatment in cancer cells reduced the activity and cleavage of USP5, a deubiquitinase (DUB) previously shown to target unanchored Ub polymers and regulate p53-mediated transcription. TRAIL was effective in suppressing USP5 activity and cleavage in TRAIL-sensitive cells but not resistant cells. Knockdown of USP5 in TRAIL-resistant cells demonstrated that USP5 controls apoptotic responsiveness to TRAIL. USP5 cleavage and ubiquitination were blocked by caspase-8 specific inhibitors. A small-molecule USP5/9× inhibitor (G9) combined with TRAIL enhanced apoptosis and blocked colony growth in highly TRAIL-resistant cell lines. Finally, USP5 protein levels and activity were found to be frequently deregulated in TRAIL-resistant cells.. hypothesis:We conclude that <el> USP5 <le> is a negative regulator of <re> TRAIL <er> responsiveness that is frequently deregulated in TRAIL-resistant cancer cells.
items.reviewed_rationale: 原研究正文支持 USP5 抑制 TRAIL 诱导凋亡，但源摘要结论句与其结果段存在方向不一致；当前 NLI premise 又未完整给出 USP5 敲低的方向结果。不能将外部正文补入题内后擅自覆盖原 negative 参考，也不足以保证所保持的具体 NLI 判断正确，撤下 R5 并禁用原参考评分。
